script: Toxic ex-boss begs me to leave a company review. I give him exactly what he asked for.. I quit my job at a small planning and design firm in Germany. The place was a mess: low pay, unpredictable leadership, and they wanted me to run a full‑blown renovation project like a seasoned project manager—without the pay or the support. Three coworkers left around the same time, and my boss had gone through five assistants in four years. I packed my bags and moved to a new city for a fresh start. A week after my last day, my former boss texted me. He casually asked, "please leave a review" for the firm on the local job review site. He thought we'd ended on good terms, so he assumed I'd drop a 5‑star rating to boost their crappy score. I rolled my eyes and ghosted him. Then it hit me: the next week, the company's page was flooded with three brand‑new 4.5‑star reviews. They were obviously faked, all posted at the same time, all using the same HR buzzwords: "great work‑life balance," "amazing health benefits," "laughing out loud." They praised everything people usually complained about. But here's the thing… I remembered his text. He wanted a review? Fine. I'd make his day. I sat down and wrote a brutally honest, mathematically precise review. I kept it professional, subjective, "In my experience…" so they couldn't sue me to take it down. I gave them 1 and 2 stars in almost every category, naming the lack of support, the horrible communication, and the heavy workload. While I was at it, I reported the three new 4.5‑star reviews to the platform's support team, pointing out the identical wording and the fact that they were posted at the exact same time. Less than four hours later, two of the three fake reviews were nuked by the platform. The automatic spam filter probably caught them because my boss had posted from the same office PC/IP address. With the fakes gone and my honest 1‑star review dragging the average down even further, panic mode set in. If this didn't work, the company could lose clients, and I might be sued for defamation—though I kept it legal. I couldn't sleep, I couldn't focus on finding a new job. His text came again, full of typos, desperately begging, "please leave a good review to help us out." He has no idea that I am the one who tanked his rating and reported his fakes. I left him on read again, because I am better than him, and he's still stuck in his little bubble. A buddy of mine who still works there texted me yesterday. He said my review hit the nail on the head and that management has suddenly been acting super nice and accommodating out of pure fear of more people quitting. The cherry on top: I've watched the company's ratings slide, the office morale dip, and the boss panic in real time. I am still sitting here, scrolling through the review page, and thinking… What do I do next? The next text just popped up…
